  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "f1",
      "concept_id": "c1",
      "text": "A checkpoint transfers WAL transactions back into the original database.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a \" checkpoint \".",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f2",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) configures databases on connection D to checkpoint after a transaction commits if the WAL contains at least N frames.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f3",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "Every new connection enables automatic checkpointing with a default threshold of 1000 pages, or the value selected by SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f4",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "Passing N less than or equal to zero to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f5",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Registering automatic checkpointing replaces an existing sqlite3_wal_hook callback, and registering a custom WAL hook disables that automatic-checkpoint mechanism.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook() . Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f6",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "Checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint use PASSIVE mode.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The wal_autocheckpoint pragma can be used to invoke this interface from SQL. Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE .",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f7",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "A checkpoint can run alongside readers but must stop upon reaching a WAL page beyond any current reader's end mark.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f8",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "A checkpoint records its progress in the wal-index and resumes from that position on its next invocation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f9",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "Overlapping readers that keep the WAL continuously in use can prevent WAL reset and allow unbounded WAL growth.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f10",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "Checkpoint starvation can be avoided by providing intervals without readers and attempting checkpoints during those intervals.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f11",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "When the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and no readers use the WAL, a writer rewinds the WAL for reuse.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f12",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "A checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file unless journal_size_limit is set.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set).",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f13",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f14",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f15",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f16",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "Under the described PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL configuration with checkpoints in a separate thread or process, transactions may roll back after a power failure or hard reset.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f17",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "By default, a threshold-triggered automatic checkpoint runs on the thread performing the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f18",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "Frequent checkpoints keep the WAL small to favor read performance.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "To maximize the read performance, one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f19",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and syncs the database if all log frames were checkpointed.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f20",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f21",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL uses busy-handler waiting for no writer and for all readers to use the latest snapshot before checkpointing all log frames and syncing the database.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f22",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "While pending, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART block new writer attempts but allow readers to proceed.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "Like SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, this mode blocks new database writer attempts while it is pending, but does not impede readers.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f23",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "After checkpointing, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART waits until all readers use only the database file, ensuring that the next writer restarts the WAL from its beginning.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f24",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE extends SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART by truncating the WAL to zero bytes immediately before a successful return.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f25",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP provides access to checkpoint counters without checkpointing any frames.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f26",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "A concurrent checkpoint in another process prevents acquisition of the checkpoint lock and causes SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f27",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE obtain an exclusive writer lock.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f28",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "If the busy handler returns zero before obtaining the writer lock or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint continues with SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f29",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "A checkpoint that falls back to PASSIVE behavior because its busy handler stops waiting returns SQLITE_BUSY.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f30",
      "concept_id": "c17",
      "text": "For non-NULL pnLog, *pnLog reports total WAL frames or -1 if an error or a database outside WAL mode prevents checkpointing.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "*pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode .",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f31",
      "concept_id": "c17",
      "text": "For non-NULL pnCkpt, *pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current call.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If pnCkpt is not NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f32",
      "concept_id": "c18",
      "text": "A NULL or empty zDb causes the requested checkpoint operation to be attempted on every WAL database attached to the connection.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f33",
      "concept_id": "c18",
      "text": "When zDb is NULL or empty and targets all attached WAL databases, the values written to *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f34",
      "concept_id": "c20",
      "text": "When the last database connection closes, it performs a final checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and associated shared-memory file.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "When the last connection to a database closes, that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file, to clean up the disk.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f35",
      "concept_id": "c19",
      "text": "The WAL cannot be reset during a write transaction, so a large write can temporarily produce a large WAL.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction. So a large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f36",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "Running checkpoints infrequently amortizes each checkpoint's cost over more writes.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "To maximize write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints infrequently",
      "pass": 0
    }
  ],
  "passes": [
    {
      "pass": 0,
      "new_claims": 36,
      "total_claims": 36,
      "new_information_rate": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "handoffs": [],
  "verdict": "BOUNDED-STAGE",
  "limitations": [
    "All three supplied sources share the sqlite.org origin; they do not satisfy the skill's independent-origin authority floor.",
    "S1 lists three checkpoint subtypes, while the mode-specific API reference S2 defines five; S2 governs the mode inventory.",
    "S1 suggests RESTART/TRUNCATE ensure completion and might block readers; S2 supplies more specific reader-concurrency rules and SQLITE_BUSY fallback conditions, which govern the claims.",
    "S1 mentions RESET without defining it, and S2 defines no corresponding mode; no separate RESET concept is inferred.",
    "The packet does not establish the historical cause of these documentation differences or provide independent disagreements or quantitative performance benchmarks.",
    "This bounded extraction does not establish research saturation."
  ]
}

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and syncs the database if all log frames were checkpointed.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL uses busy-handler waiting for no writer and for all readers to use the latest snapshot before checkpointing all log frames and syncing the database.
